items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: Remember Willie Lewis? Clarinet player -- well, he got it, and he was almost as bald as I, but he wasn't the clarinet player that I was, you know, but he got it.

ctx.x: pawn shop owner would let him come and practice every day, and it finally ended up where he was in there practicing -- the girl there talked the pawn shop broker into letting him do this. And at the end of the picture some robbers came in and robbed the pawn shop, and the clarinet player conked them on the head with the clarinet, you know.

But it was a pretty good show. Anyway, I was -- I didn't get the original show. Willie Lewis got it. Remember Willie Lewis? Clarinet player -- well, he got it, and he was almost as bald as I, but he wasn't the clarinet player that I was, you know, but he got it.

And so when they had the -- in 1960, they didn't hired me because I was bald -- so now in 1960 when they got ready to do this Angel in the Pawn Shop in summer stock in Philly at the Theater In the Round, they called me, and I did it, and I was the only one that got raving notices, you know.
